Rate limits and retries

Updated 25 October · 6 min read

Every API key has a request budget per minute. When you go over it, the API answers 429 Too Many Requests with a retry-after header that says how many seconds to wait before the next attempt.

Clients should back off exponentially and add jitter, so that a burst of failures doesn't turn into a synchronised wave of retries a few seconds later.

Free60 requests / min
Team600 requests / min
EnterpriseCustom

Choosing a retry policy

Retry only idempotent requests automatically. For writes, send an idempotency key so the server can recognise a repeated attempt and return the original result instead of applying the change twice.

Cap the total time you spend retrying. A user waiting on a page is better served by a clear error after ten seconds than by a spinner that never ends.

Monitoring

The dashboard shows your usage against the limit in one-minute buckets, and the response headers x-ratelimit-remaining and x-ratelimit-reset carry the same numbers on every request.
